claims.text: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 exhibits a large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The unchanged alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack.
The as-cast or conventionally processed alloy has a coarse-grained polycrystalline microstructure.
Controlled rolling and annealing can induce a high density of nanoscale twins in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The treatment will produce a refined microstructure with a high density of nanoscale twin boundaries.
Twin boundaries can interact with dislocations and alter deformation and local stress distributions.
Nanoscale twin boundaries will arrest or deflect crack propagation in the target alloy.
Nanoscale twin boundaries will act as stress redistributors in the target alloy.
A nano-twinned microstructure will increase the alloy's load-bearing strength relative to a conventionally processed polycrystal.
Nano-twinning will increase the yield strength of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Nano-twinning will increase the fracture toughness of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Nano-twinning will have minimal influence on the bulk phase transformations responsible for the caloric response.
The entropy change of the treated alloy will remain similar to that of the unchanged alloy.
The adiabatic temperature change of the treated alloy will remain similar to that of the unchanged alloy.
The intervention is applicable under magnetic-field and pressure-field cycling near the caloric transition temperature.
The intervention is applicable under tensile, compressive, and other service-relevant mechanical loading.
The hypothesis requires a processing window that creates nano-twins without materially altering the phase transformation.
Failure to achieve greater than 20% improvement in mechanical integrity while limiting caloric-performance loss to 10% or less would falsify the hypothesis.
